- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast peak at +3–5% above prior high.
- If supply net is strongly bearish (net < -20) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates downside; add 1–3% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.67); model often fails to revert; force 3–5% downward drift in later days if sentiment weakens.
- If 30d forecast is rising steadily (e.g., +0.5–1.0% per day), and sentiment is neutral, model often fails to account for upcoming supply events; reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3% per day.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count (≥20 events), model tends to overreact to recent auctions; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility by 10–20% in early days.
